justification: The evidence supports some attribution of operational robustness because performance remains high across multiple non-nominal conditions relevant to deployment: randomly removed non-critical fields, OCR degradation, formatting variation, three predefined perturbation tests, and an out-of-distribution test set. The reproduced validation by a separate team also strengthens the credibility of the reported results. However, the observed robustness is not uniformly strong across all stressors, and the out-of-distribution flagging rate (1,127/1,200) leaves some samples unflagged. The evidence therefore supports robustness to a meaningful extent, but not enough to treat the attribute as fully established for the deployment context from the information provided.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
An out-of-distribution test set contained 1,200 documents from document classes excluded from training.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: No explicit deployment-performance threshold is provided, so adequacy cannot be judged against a stated acceptance level.
The evidence does not specify the nature or severity of the predefined perturbations beyond the labels given.
The out-of-distribution result reports flagging counts but not downstream classification performance on unflagged samples.
The evaluation request asks about the described deployment context, but the available evidence covers only the reported validation and test conditions.
Nominal validation accuracy alone would not establish robustness; the conclusion relies on the additional perturbation and distribution-shift evidence.
